answers.answer: Yes. The primary engine will produce a joint home/away score distribution and derive spread, total, and moneyline probabilities from the same possible game outcomes.
answers.rationale: The engine exists to produce meaningful, internally coherent results that facilitate and enhance human judgment. It must expose uncertainty and relevant evidence instead of replacing judgment with a single black-box pick.
answers.author: owner
implementationEffects: Publish a central team-score forecast and a distribution around both teams' scores.
Derive spread, total, moneyline, push, and tie probabilities from the same normalized game-outcome distribution.
Show forecast uncertainty, market disagreement, source freshness, and the few evidence points that materially change the result.
Keep the model advisory: do not collapse the output into an unexplained recommendation or certainty claim.
validationRequired: Compare the joint-distribution challenger with independent market models and a power-de-vigged market baseline on identical rolling-origin rows.
Require probability calibration, score-distribution fit, and derived-market log-loss diagnostics before promotion.
Verify that every published spread, total, and moneyline probability reconciles to the same normalized score outcomes.
